title: Custodian keyflow and temporary artifact policy (draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This working draft defines an operational pattern and proposed contract language for handling temporary artifacts produced during customer POCs: ephemeral session state, transient logs, intermediate files (attachments, parsed blobs), and derived telemetry. The goal is to provide a clear, low-friction approach for pilots that balances customer privacy/legal requirements and the engineering realities of debugging and rollback during early deployments.

Key principles (operational):
- Default ephemeral: anything not explicitly requested to be retained by customer policy should be considered ephemeral and removed automatically after short TTLs.
- Custodian-separated keys: any artifacts written to persistent storage during POCs should be encrypted with a custodian key that is unique per-customer-pilot and removable on termination.
- Tiered retention by artifact type: logs/metrics < session blobs < derived datasets (e.g., aggregated QA samples). Different TTLs and scrub rules apply.
- Minimal telemetry for platform health: metrics necessary for system health are retained but stripped of user identifiers and query text by default.
- Auditable deletion: deletion operations must produce audit events and be unlinkable (cryptographically) after removal.

Artifact classification and suggested default TTLs (pilot context):
- Transient session cache (LLM KV, incomplete responses): 0–24 hours (default 2 hours).
- Temporary uploaded attachments (user files parsed by the model): 0–72 hours (default 24 hours) unless opt-in longer retention requested in contract.
- Debug snapshots (full request/response with traces): retained only when customer explicitly grants debug consent; otherwise deleted after 24 hours.
- Aggregated eval samples (anonymized prompts/responses used for quality monitoring): retained 90 days by default, anonymized on ingestion.
- System metrics and alerts: retained per platform SLOs (30 days hot, 12 months cold), with query text scrubbed.

Custodian keyflow proposal (engineer-facing):
1. Provisioning: when a POC workspace is created, generate a per-pilot envelope key (K_pilot) in the platform KMS. K_pilot is used to encrypt storage container keys (S_k).
2. Usage: S_k encrypts all persistent artifacts for that pilot. Runtime keeps S_k in memory only on nodes actively serving the pilot.
3. Rotation and revocation: provide a one-click revocation path in the Console ("Terminate pilot and destroy keys") that triggers: revoke K_pilot, zeroize S_k, and schedule garbage collection for encrypted objects (see GC section).
4. Escrow: For customers requiring escrow, support a dual-control procedure where a copy of K_pilot can be exported to a customer-managed KMS under a signed escrow agreement. Escrow copies are logged and require 2-person approval.

GC (garbage collection) considerations:
- Deletion vs. cryptographic destruction: immediate pointer removal is insufficient for regulated pilots; where required, re-encrypt object store with a new master key and securely wipe old key material.
- S3-like object stores: implement lifecycle rules plus an asynchronous shredder job responsible for chunk-level re-encryption or moving objects to a locked bucket pending secure wipe.
- Time to irrecoverability: define SLA to customer (e.g., within 72 hours after key revocation for pilot-level objects to be made cryptographically unrecoverable).

Suggested contract language (excerpt for DPA addendum):
"Temporary artifacts created solely for the purpose of conducting a pilot shall be retained only for the period expressly agreed in the pilot statement of work. By default, Redwood Inference will apply ephemeral retention policies: session caches and temporary uploads will be deleted within X days, debug snapshots will be available only with explicit consent, and platform health telemetry will be anonymized. Customers may request escrowed key custody under a mutual escrow statement; key export requires documented approval and is subject to administrative controls described in Appendix A."

Operational checklist for running a pilot under this pattern:
- [ ] Decide artifact TTLs with customer during kickoff call and record in SOW.
- [ ] Enable per-pilot KMS key generation (ENG ticket).
- [ ] Add opt-in toggle for debug snapshot retention in Console (UX ticket).
- [ ] Wire GC job to pilot lifecycle (Release/Infra ticket).
- [ ] Update on-call runbook: how to revoke a pilot and confirm cryptographic destruction.
- [ ] Legal to review the escrow clause and add Appendix A.

Open questions / risks to escalate:
- Long-running sessions (e.g., training-like workflows): our proposed short TTLs break customer expectations for multi-day contexts. Need product decision whether to support extended session persistence for certain pilots and what guardrails (billing, isolation) are required.
- Cost/operational overhead of per-pilot encryption keys and frequent re-encryption on key revocation. Engineering estimate required (see linked PR).
- For customers in high-regulation geos, do we need physical wipe or just cryptographic unrecoverability? Align with security/compliance.
- UX friction: how will support troubleshoot incidents if debug snapshots default to off? Consider controlled opt-in with time-limited access.

Notes from recent workshop (2/20/2025):
- Customer asked for a "writable ephemeral sandbox" where they can replay sessions for debugging without exposing raw user inputs to our engineers. Proposed approach: provide a redacted replay artifact generated by customer-owned tokenization/redaction hooks before storage.
- Solutions and SRE agree to prototype a console flow for key revocation and destruction audit trail.
- Legal wants a short, prescriptive DPA paragraph rather than long appendices for pilots.

Next steps (owner: Ayesha Patel):
- Get engineering estimates for KMS per-pilot cost and GC implementation (due 2025-03-09).
- Draft a short DPA paragraph and Appendix A for escrow controls (Legal pinged, due 2025-03-05).
- Add a small UX prototype for debug opt-in and a one-click termination button on staging (Design + Eng sync 2025-02-28).

Appendix: quick decision log
- 2025-02-14: Decided default TTLs (session 2h, attachments 24h) for initial pilots.
- 2025-02-20: Customer asked for redacted replay capability (see workshop notes).
- 2025-02-25: Engineering prefers cryptographic destruction over physical wipe for most cloud pilots; raise to Compliance for final approval.

Unresolved: precise language for "anonymized" vs "redacted" in telemetry; Legal to propose definitive terms.

Tagline for the SOW: "Pilot-safe defaults for data minimization: ephemeral by default, auditable when required."

End of draft.

(Notes-to-self: link sample SOW snippet to Confluence; schedule demo of key revocation flow with SRE)
